summary: Autonomous Chaos Engineering audit completed across 3 microservice targets. The architecture demonstrated an overall resilience score of 38/100. The automated safety watchdog successfully guarded all tests, preventing catastrophic system crashes. Key vulnerabilities identified in synchronous cart dependency and catalog response throttling.

vulnerabilities.title: Cascading Outage on Cart Dependency Outage
vulnerabilities.description: Frontend lacks local session storage or circuit-breaking for cart operations. Unavailability of cart container halts user shopping workflow and propagates 5xx errors.
vulnerabilities.impact: Severe direct checkout and revenue loss; storefront degraded.

vulnerabilities.title: Stateful Redis/Valkey Session Datastore SPOF
vulnerabilities.description: Cart service has a direct, hard synchronous dependency on valkey-cart. When the session datastore is unavailable, all cart operations hang and throw timeouts.
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete loss of customer cart sessions and checkout initiation.

vulnerabilities.title: Non-Critical Service Degradation Blast Radius
vulnerabilities.description: Service recommendation disruption induced MTTR of 0.51s before telemetry stabilized back to baseline.
vulnerabilities.impact: Subsystem delay without immediate catastrophic outage.

prescribed_fixes.recommendation: Implement an Envoy/gRPC circuit breaker between frontend and cart. Fallback to client-side localStorage or read-only cart view with asynchronous queueing for pending add-to-cart events.

prescribed_fixes.fix_type: Redis Sentinel Replication & In-Memory Fallback Cache
prescribed_fixes.recommendation: Deploy Valkey/Redis in high-availability mode with Sentinel replication. Equip cart service with an in-process LRU cache for read degradation when Valkey is unreachable.
Wrap recommendation calls in non-blocking async promises with empty fallbacks and exponential backoff retry policies.
